Tidy and glance methods for sdid results

Source: R/tidy.R
sdid-tidiers.Rd

Summaries of the result of sdid() in the form the broom package defines, which modelsummary and other packages for tables of estimates use. tidy() gives a row per estimate and glance() one row describing the data. The methods become available once the generics package is loaded, as it is by modelsummary and broom, so modelsummary(fit) works without further setup. Arguments given to modelsummary that it does not use itself, such as cohorts and labels, are passed on to tidy().

# S3 method for class 'sdid'
tidy(
  x,
  conf.int = TRUE,
  conf.level = x$level/100,
  cohorts = FALSE,
  labels = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'sdid'
glance(x, ...)

Arguments

x

The result of sdid().

conf.int

TRUE (the default) to include the bounds of the confidence interval.

conf.level

The confidence level of the interval, as a proportion. Defaults to the level of the fit. modelsummary sets it from its conf_level argument.

cohorts

TRUE to add a row for each adoption period of a staggered design, after the overall effect. Defaults to FALSE. A design with a single adoption period gets no further rows.

labels

Optional names for all the rows, in order, the overall effect first and then, with cohorts = TRUE, each adoption period. By default the overall effect is named by the treatment column and each cohort by its adoption period.

...

Not used.

Value

tidy() returns a data frame with a row per estimate and the columns term, the row's name, estimate, std.error, statistic, the z statistic, p.value, its p-value under the standard normal distribution against the fit's alternative, and, with conf.int = TRUE, conf.low and conf.high, one of which is infinite for a one-sided alternative. Without inference the standard errors and everything computed from them are NA. glance() returns a data frame with one row and the columns nobs, the number of observations, n.units, the number of units, n.periods, the number of periods, and covariates, the names of the covariates separated by commas, or NA without covariates.

Examples

# \donttest{
data(california_prop99)
fit = sdid(california_prop99, "PacksPerCapita", "State", "Year",
           "treated", vce = "placebo", seed = 1213, graph = FALSE,
           quietly = TRUE)
if (requireNamespace("generics", quietly = TRUE)) {
  generics::tidy(fit)
  generics::glance(fit)
}
#>   nobs n.units n.periods covariates
#> 1 1209      39        31       <NA>
# }
